newsitem.title: USA: Clinton hails Mexico's early loan repayment.
newsitem.headline: Clinton hails Mexico's early loan repayment.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Wednesday hailed Mexico's early repayment of its emergency loan to the U.S. Treasury, saying it was a tribute to Mexico's economic recovery and vindicated his decision to help the country out of its financial crisis two years ago.

"In 1995, when my administration put together this emergency support package, Mexico was in crisis," Clinton said at a White House event. "Today the United States is being repaid more than three years ahead of schedule, we have earned more than half a billion dollars on our loan, our exports to Mexico are at an all-time high and the Mexican economy is back on track."

"Two years ago helping our friend and neighbor in a time of need was quite controversial," Clinton said. "Some said that we should not get involved, that the money would never be repaid, that Mexico should fend for itself. They were wrong."

Clinton said the United States would continue to support Mexico's reforms and that he hoped to visit the country "quite soon." U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said Mexico had accomplished a great deal but still had much to do.

Earlier, Mexican Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz said Mexico would immediately repay the outstanding $3.5 billion of an emergency loan from the U.S. Treasury and would also repay early $1.5 billion owed to the International Monetary Fund.

In 1995 Clinton came under severe criticism, particularly from Republicans, for the Mexican aid package. When initially announced, it amounted to nearly $50 billion, including up to $20 billion from the United States, $17.8 billion from the IMF and $10 billion from other industrial nations.
